sub_palette: old_persian (Indo-Iranian; a distinct register layered over the near_eastern theonym base)
_note: Single-source (Achaemenid Persia, §5.1 #21). A tolerant satrapal empire of the forested uplands and the steppe: high stability, soft 'fading' degradation rather than hard collapse. Old Persian (Indo-Iranian) phonology and the real satrapal/Old-Persian rulership register (Xshayathiya, Xshacapavan/satrap, Marzapana, Bandaka - allowed, catalog 5.3). DEITY names START from the Sargonid set (the Akkadian-canon morphs of the Agrippan pantheon) and are SHIFTED into the Old Persian register (per Jedidiah): Tullaru -> Turvasa, Urlandu -> Urlaspa, Numunu -> Naumana, Argantu -> Arzanta, Itarnu -> Asturna. Never real Iranian/Zoroastrian holy names (no Ahura Mazda, Mithra, etc.). The cardinal virtue is ARTA (Truth/Right-order); its opposite is DRAUGA (the Lie). Honesty-as-paramount is carried by Arta-theophorics and NPC personality weighting, not a new value-enum entry. The empire is religiously TOLERANT: the King of Kings shelters the subject cults under Asturna's peace.

phonology.palette: Old Persian (Indo-Iranian): vowels a i u with long a/i/u; spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f; sibilants s/sh/z/zh and c(ts); r l; nasals m n; semivowels y v/w; aspirate h; characteristic endings -a, -ah, -ish, -iya, -ana, -aspa(horse), -arta(truth), -data(law-given), -farnah(glory); theophoric stems are the Old-Persian-shifted canon morphs (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-, Baga-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C); permitted clusters xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, vr-, thr-; vowel length distinctive; stress on heavy syllables; the genitive-of-relation '-ahya'.

morphology.patronymic_form: filiation 'X-ahya puthra' (son of X) or compact 'X-puthra'; theophoric given names on the shifted god-stems and on Arta- (Truth); nobles a house (vith-X) or a chiliad; no inherited surname for commoners (filiation + earned epithet).
morphology.compounding_rule: quality/relation + element: Arta-xshaca (truth-realm), Vahu-farnah (good-glory), Baga-data (god-given); construct via '-ahya'; toponyms Dida-[name] (fort of), [name]-pura (city of), Atash-[power] (fire of).

title_ladder.government: imperial bureaucracy - the satrapal empire: the Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) over the satraps (Xshacapavan), the chiliarch-vizier (Hazarapatish), the royal road and the king's-eye inspectors; the magi tend the fire but seldom rule.
title_ladder._tiers_note: Old Persian, ascending. Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden, the marzban) march; Framatar (appointed director/governor) county over a Parada (governed district); Xshacapavan (SATRAP, protector of the realm) duchy over a satrapy; Vispuhra (prince of the blood) principality over a great province (Dahyu); Xshayathiya (king) kingdom; Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. (Rank titles are the real Old-Persian/satrapal register, allowed.)
title_ladder.heir: Mathishta (the greatest; crown prince) / Visa-puthra (the king's son)

vassalage.tribute: Baji (tribute) / Bara (the gift borne to the king)

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric or Arta-/Vahu- virtue-name) + filiation (X-puthra); nobles add a house (vith-X) and a court/satrapal office; the renowned earn an honest-deed epithet.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the court-and-satrapal nobility carry a house (vith) and office; commoners use filiation + earned epithet.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names from the shifted deity-stems + an Old Persian element: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Vahu-X (good-X). e.g. Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah, Vahu-Arzanta.

religion._note: Deity-names START from the Sargonid set (Akkadian-canon morphs of the Agrippan pantheon) and are SHIFTED into Old Persian phonology (Tullaru -> Turvasa, Urlandu -> Urlaspa, Numunu -> Naumana, Argantu -> Arzanta, Rialtu -> Riyata, Itarnu -> Asturna), recognizably the same powers, never real Iranian/Zoroastrian gods. Lawful henotheist but TOLERANT: Asturna the Wise Lord most high upholds ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and the Lawful powers are His yazata-ministers; the Chaotic powers are the hosts of DRAUGA (the Lie). The cardinal sin is the Lie; the king's word is bond. The empire shelters the cults of its subject peoples under Asturna's peace - foreign gods are tolerated in the satrapies, never suppressed.
religion.the_one: Asturna (< Aeternus / Sargonid Itarnu; the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the king's farnah-glory, revered above His ministers)

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Turvasa (the sun and Arta, lamp of right-order; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Naumana (the good mind, wisdom and the law; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlaspa (the iron-oath, war and the cavalier; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Argentus: Arzanta (trade, the road and increase; Lawful)
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (the Lady of Waters, mother and mercy)

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers are the hosts of Drauga the Lie, each keeping its shifted name + a hostile portfolio-epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities; Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void; Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent (the Lie made gold).

clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (the chief of chief magi)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atash ([fire] of [power]) and its fire-temple (Atashana): 'the Atashana of Turvasa'; the magi keep the ever-burning fire (Atar) on the altar.
religion.saints_pattern: the honest dead and the just kings, kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and petitioned at the fire-altar; 'the Arta-true [name]' (the righteous [name]).

holy_symbol_motifs.Asturna: a winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory) above a fire-altar
holy_symbol_motifs.Turvasa: a rayed sun above the upright Arta-measure
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlaspa: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring

banks_patterns.ships: royal-road and river-barge names (a land-empire's few craft): 'Bearer of the Baji', 'the Farnah', 'Boat of Arzanta'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [number/power] Spada (host) and the Immortal-style guard: 'the Spada of Urlaspa', 'the Ten-Thousand (Anushiya)'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: fallen apadana-halls and dead fire-temples: 'the dead Atashana of [name]', 'the buried Apadana of Dida-[name]'
